Inspect factual study capabilities

Source: R/study.R
study_capabilities.Rd

Reports what the binding actually established, so downstream calls can require a guarantee instead of assuming it.

Usage

study_capabilities(x)

Arguments

x

An study().

Value

A one-row data frame with logical columns aligned_observations, timing_resolved, partition_hierarchy, and stable_source_revision.

See also

study(), and compiler_conformance() for the equivalent report on a compiled relation plan.

Other studies and effect maps: coefficient_parameterization(), condition_space(), design_model(), effect_map(), effect_space(), lower_effect_map(), observation_model(), raw_design_model(), raw_effect_map(), study(), study_axis()

Examples

set.seed(1)
domain <- abstract_domain(4L, id = "study-capabilities-example")
index <- observation_index(
  1:6, "run-1", time = seq(0, 10, by = 2), units = "seconds"
)
record <- observations(
  list(`run-1` = matrix(rnorm(24), 6L, 4L)), list(`run-1` = index), domain
)

# With no event record there is no timing to resolve, and the report says so
# rather than defaulting to TRUE.
study_capabilities(study(record))
#>   aligned_observations timing_resolved partition_hierarchy
#> 1                 TRUE           FALSE                TRUE
#>   stable_source_revision
#> 1                   TRUE

# Binding timed events on the same clock earns `timing_resolved`.
events <- observation_events(data.frame(
  partition = "run-1", event_id = c("e1", "e2"), onset = c(0, 6),
  duration = 0.5
))
study_capabilities(study(record, events))$timing_resolved
#> [1] TRUE
